gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now keeps the existing gpio_wdt lane, the new bcm2835_wdt starter tests, and the bcm2835 survey checkpoint reviewable together so the watchdog tranche does not drift across simple-driver anchors.

A dedicated survey gate still matters after the starter lands because it keeps the remaining bcm2835_wdt gap explicit instead of letting the new scaffold imply platform or hardware parity that has not been implemented.
The survey note now records that the first bcm2835_wdt starter has landed while the next bounded step remains probe summary and registration-facing bookkeeping only.

The bounded starter now covers timeout tick encoding, running-bit detection, start and stop register transitions, restart intent, and halt-partition bookkeeping without claiming platform-backed behavior.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep timeout conversion, restart intent, halt-partition bookkeeping, and bounded register-image transitions reviewable without pretending hardware-backed execution exists.
A dedicated slice note now documents exactly what the first Zig starter covers and what remains out of scope so the repo does not conflate the starter with full platform or poweroff integration.

The next honest bounded step is a tiny probe-time summary around bootloader-carried running state, heartbeat and nowayout initialization, restart priority, and watchdog parent linkage before any platform registration or MMIO-backed behavior.

Platform registration, PM base acquisition, the system power controller path, and live poweroff-handler coordination remain blocked until the lane has a small probe summary plus a hardware-validation matrix that can describe those side effects honestly.
